text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS

-- National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh has welcomed the intention of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the Asian Inter-Parliamentary Organisation (AIPO) to include Laos, Cambodia and Burma as members in the near future.
-- The death toll from last week's tropical depression that hit four central coast provinces has risen to 33, the Central Committee for Floods and Storms Control said.
-- Many Vietnamese children begin school later than the compulsory age of six, a government study on edication showed.

-- Most Official Development Aid (ODA) in Vietnam has been used to develop transport infrastructure. Twenty-six of 47 ODA projects have been completed, with investment capital estimated at about $1.283 billion.

-- French hotel developer Compagnie Generale de Batiment et de Construction has missed a chance to accomodate heads of state who are expected in Hanoi for the seventh Francophone summit at the end of next year. Its Hanoi Opera Hilton joint venture five-star hotel will not be ready on time. - - - - LE COURRIER DU VIETNAM
-- Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum in Hanoi will be closed from October 4 to December 2 for renovation.
-- Haiphong's Cat Bi airport has reopened again after a year-long revamp. - - - -
NHAN DAN
-- The government has worked out eight resolutions for the socio-economic development of the country's highland areas.

-- Implementing the second stage of a drive against "social evils", Ho Chi Minh City authorities have so far this year seized 132,171 video tapes and 59,114 books, pulled down 369 illegal advertising billboards and 8,088 signs. They also arrested 764 prositutes, 379 drug addicts and 1,160 beggars and homeless people.

-- Framework agreements were signed between Vietnam's government, the North-Europe Investment Bank and the North-Europe Development Fund. By signing the agreements Vietnam officially established relations with multilateral financial organizations from Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland and Iceland. - - - -
QUAN DOI NHAN DAN
-- Vietnam Veterans of America (VVA) and the Vietnam Veterans Association agreed to continue cooperation on MIA issues during VVA President James Brazee's visit to Hanoi last week.
-- Rice fields and houses were destroyed by three elephants in the highland province of DakLak last week. - - - -
HA NOI MOI

-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment licensed a $5 joint-venture linking Japan's Takanachi and Mitsui companies and Vietnam's Xuan Hoa company to produce car interior parts. The plant's production will be used by Toyota factory in Vinh Phu province.
-- A conference on the establishment of trade unions in companies with foreign investment was held by the Hanoi People's Committee.
-- A nationwide competition on traffic safety was launched by the ministries of transport, interior and education and training and the Communist Youth League.
